newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ monetary conditions index falls in Nov - BTNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ monetary conditions index falls in Nov - BTNZ.

text.p: Bankers Trust New Zealand said on Tuesday its monetary conditions index fell to average 133.5 in November from 137 in October.
The lower MCI was entirely due to lower average 90-day interest rates -- 9.0 percent vs 9.6 percent.
The average of the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index was actually higher in November, at 67.3 vs 66.9.

"The market is pricing in an easing of monetary conditions in the (Reserve Bank's) December Monetary Policy Statement," BTNZ said. A drop in 90-day interest rates had seen the MCI fall to 127 since the end of November, it said.
The assumed MCI level for the December quarter, based on the Reserve Bank's September projections is 126.
BTNZ said economic data pointing to an improved inflaltion outlook justified a monetary policy easing.
The RB had allowed 90-day bill rates to fall one percentage point below their October 16 level when the bank said a further easing would be inappropriate.
"We think this reflects the subdued tone of the recent economic data," chief economist David Plank said.
The mix of conditions had changed, with the currency largely holding its value.
BTNZ said it believed the market had fully priced in any easing sought by the RB.
BTNZ believed the RB would assume 90-day bills at 8.5 percent and a Trade-Weighted Index starting point of 66.0-66.5 in its December forecasts, due on December 17.
BTNZ said that if it became clear a new government would substantially loosen fiscal policy, then the RB would be reluctant to sanction the market's easing so far.

An announcement on a government coalition is expected within the next 10 days after protracted negotiations since a general election on October 12. The conservative National Party and centre-left Labour are both trying to form a government with the support of nationalist New Zealand First.
